steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Combine pumpkin, evaporated milk, sugar, eggs, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a large bowl; mix well. Spread batter in the prepared pan.
Sprinkle cake mix over pumpkin batter; pat down gently. Sprinkle chopped pecans evenly over cake; drizzle with butter.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, and a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean, 60 to 80 minutes.
Let cake cool; spread with whipped topping.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Crunch Cake
raw_recipe.description: This pumpkin crunch cake recipe is a classic dump cake made with canned pumpkin, cake mix, and pecans for a sweet, buttery dessert perfect for fall.

review.reviewBody: WOW !!! I made this cake at Thanksgiving dinner at my in-laws and it was such a success I think this may be my staple contribution each year. I took someone's suggestion on toasting the pecans in butter before adding it to the cake and instead of margarine, I used unsalted butter (since one person said the cake was somewhat salty). Instead of using whipped cream - I made crumb cake crumbs and baked them on during the last 15 minutes of baking (to make crumbs: use 2 1/2 cup flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 2 tsp vanilla, 2 tsp cinnamon 1 1/2 stick unsalted butter melted - I mixed them all together with my hands and put them on top of the pecan/pumpkin/cake mixture). The crumbs, buttery pecans, cake mix & pumpkin mixture was so unbelievable (although filling) everyone raved about it !!!! I think next year though I will cut back on the sugar and butter as it is such a sweet cake and rich cake having one sliver is almost too much to eat and there's no room for other desserts ! Thank you for this superb recipe !!! YUMMMM !
I've made this for years but substitute Pumpkin Pie Mix for the Pure Pumpkin - It comes out perfect every time! I also invert the Cake onto a platter so that the Pecans form a crust for the cake :-D
Great recipe, but too sweet and not enough pecans... if you reduce the sugar by half and double your pecans it's glorious. For my oven, it was best to reduce the heat and cook for an hour twenty.

MUST use margarine (not butter ) & NOT over-cook for top to be right. It is also best to cut into servings while still warm. I also decreased the sugar in half. With the cake mix on top, it only needs at the most 1 cup. (This is pumpkin pie recipe with double eggs and sugar.) I have made this recipe multiple times and made the top too tough by using butter instead of margarine. Even our biggest sweet-tooth says it is too sweet at the amount of sugar in recipe. It really needs the topping or whip cream to complete.

This Pumpkin Crunch was very good. I did modify the recipe a little. I used a 30oz can of Pumpkin Puree in stead of only 15oz. I didn't put pumpkin spice, but used cinnamon in its place and I didn't use salt. I lined my cake pan with wax paper and once the crunch was completely cooled, flipped it over onto a decorative tray so that the "crust" would be on the bottom. I used a large container of whipped topping and frosted the top. Simply delicious! Everyone at the office loved it. I will be using this recipe again.

Absolutely love this cake. Took advice from other reviews. Used spice cake instead of yellow cake. Put pecans through coffee grinder, and mixed them in the spice cake. This released the oils from the pecans and gave a real rich nutty flavor. Put about 1/2 of a cup chocolate chips in the freezer. Then, put them through coffee, grinder and topped the cake with them. It looked like a lot, however, you could not taste the chocolate that much. Next time I will put more. I'm thinking of using the spice cake part of this recipe for the crust of my pumpkin pies. That was a suggestion from one of my guests at my barbecue/bonfire, I had when I served this cake. If I do that, I will mix the butter into the spice cake so it mixes evenly and then press into pie PAN.. I was thinking of doing deep dish, so I'll have room for the whipped cream cheese, topping sprinkled with chocolate.

This came out really great, even though I forgot to drizzle the butter until 20 min. before the cake was done. I also only used 2/3 c. butter, and also shorted the sugar. To top this, we melted half a can of cream cheese frosting and drizzled it on top of the slightly cooled cake (as one reviewer suggested -- thanks!). We also didn't use nuts because some people are picky. So, basically, you can forget stuff and short ingredients and it's still delicious!

Pretty good, but needed adjustments. Made another pan with 1 less egg and 1/2 cup less sugar. 
The 2nd pan was the winner!

Made this for a function at our church. I can honestly it was a success. Will definitely be making this again. I did sauté the chopped pecans in butter that someone suggested and for my topping instead of cool whip I used the suggestion of another reviewer: container of cool whip, 8oz cream cheese softened and 1/2 cup powdered sugar mixed well. It’s a keeper in our family.
Way way to much sugar! Use a quarter cup brown sugar and that's plenty. I made it per the directions first. It was much better the next time around with 1/4 cup brown sugar.

This is just for the filling I am not rating the whole recipe, because I only use the pumpkin filling part of this recipe. I make a spice cake base similar to a gooey butter cake, layer with this filling, and apply a streusel topping using butter, sugar, and quick rolled oats for any nuts used in the topping. Then I top it off with a buttercream:)
I have made this recipe in the Fall for years. Excellent recipe. Definitely a family favorite!
This recipe has been a staple for our holiday dinners for many years - so yummy!
Do you sprinkle the dried cake mix over it or do you make the cake according to directions on the cake mix and put it over the top before baking?
Very yummy, didn't change anything, everyone loved it
Great with vanilla Ice cream too. Love this recipe 😋
Followed instructions. Pumpkin was a little runny. I did only bake for 60 minutes. But delicious and will definitely make it again!

It’s our family’s favorite and become a tradition for me to make! I make a version without pecans for my kids, but I put extra on mine! We always make it a day ahead of time because we all agree it’s best served cold with cool whip - more cohesive and just better tasting!
only used 3/4 cup sugar, it was fine

I substituted yellow cake mix with butter pecan cake mix - Yummy! I also drizzled caramel sauce over the cool whip when serving pieces of this dessert. I accidentally set the oven at 375 degrees - after about 48 minutes I noticed my pecans were getting toasty and then I noticed my temp error. I immediately removed the pan and set it on a cooling rack. Fortunately, it turned out perfect!
